functions.name: gettime
functions.signature: extern int gettime(struct timespec* tp, bool needRealTime = false);
functions.description: Populates the provided struct timespec with a system time value. Based on the name and boolean parameter, this function likely wraps a system clock query (for example choosing between a monotonic clock and the real-time clock) and stores the result in tp. Usage: pass a writable timespec pointer; set needRealTime to true if wall-clock (real) time is desired, otherwise leave default (likely monotonic time). Return value is an int; the exact success/error convention is not specified in this header, so callers should check and handle nonzero/negative returns as errors. Notes: Declared with external linkage; actual behavior may vary per platform depending on implementation in the corresponding source file.
requirements: tp must be a non-null pointer to writable memory referencing a valid struct timespec.
Callers should include a definition of struct timespec (for example by including <time.h> or <ctime>) before using this API.
Callers must check the returned int for success or failure; exact semantics are not defined in this header, so treat nonzero/negative values as errors as appropriate for the implementation.
needRealTime controls which clock is used; details are not specified here, but by convention false likely means a monotonic clock and true means wall-clock (real) time.
